questions.question: Which of the following classes has the largest number of animals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insects**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insects** have the largest number of animals among all classes.
 
• Insects belong to the class **Insecta** within the phylum **Arthropoda**.
 
• This class includes diverse species such as **beetles, butterflies, bees, ants, and flies**.
 
• Insects are characterized by having a **three-part body structure** (head, thorax, abdomen), **compound eyes**, and **one pair of antennae**.
 
• They play crucial roles in ecosystems, including **pollination, decomposition, and serving as a food source** for other animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The class **Insecta** is the most diverse group of animals on Earth, with an estimated **millions of species**.
 
• Insects are found in nearly all environments on the planet, from **forests and deserts to freshwater and even marine environments**.
 
• The study of insects is known as **entomology**.
 
• Insects have been around for over **400 million years**, making them one of the oldest groups of animals.
 
• They have a significant impact on human activities, both positive (e.g., pollination of crops) and negative (e.g., pests).

questions.question: On 7th March 2022, the Government initiated a scheme to re-enrol out-of-school adolescent girls (OoS AG) in the age group of 11-14 years. What is the name of the scheme?

options.text: National Scheme of Incentives to Girls for Secondary Education

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanya Shiksha Pravesh Utsav**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Government of India initiated the **Kanya Shiksha Pravesh Utsav** scheme on 7th March 2022.
 
• This scheme aims to re-enrol out-of-school adolescent girls (OoS AG) in the age group of 11-14 years.
 
• The initiative is part of the efforts to ensure that every girl child has access to education and to reduce the dropout rate among adolescent girls.
 
• It targets girls who have left school before completing their education, providing them with an opportunity to continue their studies.
 
• The scheme also focuses on creating awareness about the importance of girls' education and aims to remove the socio-economic barriers that prevent girls from attending school.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The scheme is implemented in collaboration with the Ministry of Education and other relevant stakeholders.
 
• Special focus is given to marginalized sections of society to ensure inclusivity in education.
 
• Various incentives and support mechanisms are provided to encourage the enrolment and retention of girls in schools.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India states about the executive power of the Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 53**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 53** of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of the Union shall be vested in the President.
 
• The President can exercise these powers either directly or through officers subordinate to him in accordance with the Constitution.
 
• This article is a part of the larger framework that outlines the powers and duties of the executive branch of the government.
 
• It ensures that the executive authority is centralized under the President, thereby providing a unified command structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **President of India** is the head of state and the supreme commander of the armed forces.
 
• The President is elected by an electoral college comprising the elected members of both houses of Parliament and the legislative assemblies of states and union territories.
 
• The executive power extends to the matters with respect to which Parliament has the power to make laws and to the exercise of such rights, authority, and jurisdiction as are exercisable by the Government of India by virtue of any treaty or agreement.
 
• The President also has the power to appoint the Prime Minister, who acts as the head of government, and other ministers based on the Prime Minister's advice.
 
• The Constitution of India provides a detailed framework for the distribution of powers between the executive, legislative, and judiciary branches to ensure a balanced governance structure.

questions.question: From the given alternatives, identify an inner planet.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mercury**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mercury** is classified as an inner planet in our solar system.
 
• The inner planets, also known as terrestrial planets, include **Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars**.
 
• These planets are characterized by their rocky surfaces and are located closer to the Sun compared to the outer planets.
 
• Mercury is the smallest and closest planet to the Sun, with a very thin atmosphere and extreme temperature variations.
 
• It has no moons or rings and completes an orbit around the Sun in just 88 Earth days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mercury** was named after the Roman messenger god due to its swift orbit around the Sun.
 
• It has a heavily cratered surface, similar to Earth's Moon, and experiences drastic changes in temperature, ranging from -173°C at night to 427°C during the day.
 
• The planet's thin atmosphere, known as an exosphere, is composed mostly of oxygen, sodium, hydrogen, helium, and potassium.
 
• Mercury's magnetic field is about 1% the strength of Earth's, and it has a large iron core that generates this field.
 
• Space missions such as **Mariner 10** and **MESSENGER** have provided valuable information about Mercury's characteristics and surface.

questions.question: The term ‘bishop’ is associated with which game?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**chess**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'bishop'** is associated with the game of **chess**.
 
• In chess, the bishop is a piece that moves diagonally across the board.
 
• Each player starts with two bishops, one on a light square and one on a dark square.
 
• The bishop can move any number of squares diagonally, but cannot jump over other pieces.
 
• The bishop is considered a minor piece in the game of chess, alongside the knight.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chess is a two-player strategy board game played on an 8x8 grid.
 
• Each player begins with 16 pieces: one king, one queen, two rooks, two knights, two bishops, and eight pawns.
 
• The objective of chess is to checkmate the opponent's king, putting it under threat of capture with no legal moves to escape.
 
• Chess is believed to have originated in India during the Gupta Empire, where it was known as Chaturanga.
 
• The modern rules of chess were standardized in the 19th century.

questions.question: From which country were the ideals of justice of the Indian Constitution borrowed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The USSR**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer is **The USSR**__.
 
• The ideals of justice in the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of the USSR.
 
• These ideals include social, economic, and political justice which aim to create a fair and equitable society.
 
• The concept of justice in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in the Preamble and forms a part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the longest written constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.
 
• The Preamble to the Constitution reflects the aspirations and objectives of the Constitution, including justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity.
 
• Justice in the Indian context is not limited to legal justice but also includes social and economic dimensions.

questions.question: The festival of Eid Milad-un-Nabi is celebrated in which of the following Islamic months?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rabi' al-Awwal**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid Milad-un-Nabi** is celebrated in the Islamic month of **Rabi' al-Awwal**.
 
• Rabi' al-Awwal is the third month in the **Islamic calendar**.
 
• This festival commemorates the **birth of the Prophet Muhammad**, who is considered the last prophet in Islam.
 
• It is a significant event for Muslims around the world, who engage in various religious activities such as **prayers, recitations, and gatherings** to honor the Prophet's life and teachings.
 
• The exact date of celebration may vary based on the sighting of the moon, as the Islamic calendar is **lunar-based**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Islamic calendar, also known as the **Hijri calendar**, began in 622 AD when Prophet Muhammad migrated from Mecca to Medina, an event known as the **Hijra**.
 
• The calendar consists of 12 months and is approximately **10-12 days shorter** than the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Other significant months in the Islamic calendar include **Muharram, Ramadan, and Dhul-Hijjah**, each with its own religious importance.
 
• Muslims around the world follow the Islamic calendar for **religious observances**, including fasting during Ramadan and performing the Hajj pilgrimage.

questions.question: In which Harappan site was a paved bathroom found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohenjodaro**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A paved bathroom was discovered at the Harappan site of **Mohenjodaro**.
 
• Mohenjodaro is one of the major urban centers of the Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The city is known for its advanced urban planning, including well-organized streets, drainage systems, and sophisticated water management.
 
• The discovery of a paved bathroom indicates the importance of hygiene and sanitation in the Harappan culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjodaro** was discovered by R. D. Banerji in 1922.
 
• The site is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is considered one of the world's earliest major urban settlements.
 
• Excavations have revealed that Mohenjodaro had a complex social structure, advanced engineering, and a high standard of living.
 
• The city's name means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
• Other significant features of Mohenjodaro include the Great Bath, granary, and the assembly hall.
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, to which Mohenjodaro belongs, flourished around 2500 BCE to 1900 BCE.

questions.question: In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru, president of Indian National Congress, formally demanded __________ from British Government.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**complete freedom**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru, as the president of the Indian National Congress, formally demanded **complete freedom** from the British Government.
 
• This demand marked a significant shift from the previous demand for dominion status to the more radical goal of complete independence.
 
• The resolution for complete freedom was passed during the Lahore session of the Indian National Congress in 1929.
 
• This session is also notable for the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the ultimate goal of the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• The Indian National Congress decided to observe 26th January 1930 as Independence Day, which later became the date when the Constitution of India came into effect in 1950.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The demand for complete freedom was a turning point in the Indian freedom struggle, galvanizing the Indian populace and intensifying the fight against British colonial rule.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru's leadership during this period played a crucial role in uniting various factions within the Congress and presenting a united front against the British.
 
• The Lahore session also saw the adoption of the tricolor as the national flag of India.
 
• This period marked the beginning of a series of civil disobedience movements and protests that eventually led to India gaining independence in 1947.
 
• Jawaharlal Nehru later became the first Prime Minister of independent India, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.

questions.question: Thaneswar where the Vardhana dynasty ruled around the present-day state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haryana**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Thaneswar, where the Vardhana dynasty ruled, is located in the present-day state of **Haryana**.
 
• The Vardhana dynasty, also known as the Pushyabhuti dynasty, was prominent in northern India during the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• Harsha, one of the most notable rulers of this dynasty, played a significant role in unifying northern India during his reign.
 
• Thaneswar served as the capital of the Vardhana dynasty under King Harsha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Vardhana dynasty came to prominence after the decline of the Gupta Empire.
 
• King Harsha, also known as Harshavardhana, was a patron of arts and culture and established a large empire in northern India.
 
• Harsha's reign is well documented in the accounts of the Chinese traveler Xuanzang, who visited India during Harsha's rule.
 
• Thaneswar, now known as Kurukshetra, is a city of great historical and religious significance in India.

questions.question: Technetium, the first artificially produced element used in many medical diagnostic imaging scans, is found in which group of the periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Group 7**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Technetium is a chemical element with the symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
 
• It is the first element to be artificially produced and is primarily used in medical diagnostic imaging scans.
 
• Technetium is found in **Group 7** of the periodic table.
 
• Elements in Group 7 are known as transition metals and share similar properties.
 
• Technetium is unique among the first 82 elements in that it has no stable isotopes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Technetium was discovered by Carlo Perrier and Emilio Segrè in 1937.
 
• Its most common isotope, Technetium-99m, is widely used in nuclear medicine for a variety of diagnostic tests, including imaging of the heart, bones, and other organs.
 
• Technetium is produced in nuclear reactors and is a byproduct of fission in nuclear reactors and weapons.
 
• It is also used in corrosion-resistant alloys and as a tracer in hydrology.

questions.question: K-selected species are characterised by:

options.text: species possessing relatively stable populations and which tend to produce relatively low numbers of offspring
species possessing relatively unstable populations and which tend to produce relatively large numbers of offspring
species possessing relatively unstable populations and which tend to produce relatively low numbers of offspring
species possessing relatively stable populations and which tend to produce relatively large numbers of offspring

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**species possessing relatively stable populations and which tend to produce relatively low numbers of offspring **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **K-selected species** are characterised by species possessing relatively stable populations and which tend to produce relatively low numbers of offspring.
 
• These species typically have longer lifespans, delayed maturity, and significant parental care.
 
• They thrive in stable environments where competition for resources is high.
 
• Examples of K-selected species include elephants, humans, and many large mammals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **R-selected species**, in contrast, possess relatively unstable populations and tend to produce large numbers of offspring with minimal parental care.
 
• The concept of r/K selection theory was developed to describe the reproductive strategies of different organisms.
 
• K-selected species are usually more affected by environmental changes due to their longer life cycles and lower reproductive rates.
 
• Conservation efforts often focus on K-selected species due to their vulnerability to habitat destruction and other human activities.

questions.question: The first train steamed off from Mumbai to ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thane**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thane** was the destination of the first train that steamed off from Mumbai.
 
• This historic journey took place on **16th April 1853**.
 
• The train covered a distance of **34 kilometers** from Mumbai to Thane.
 
• This event marked the beginning of the railway system in India.
 
• The train was operated by the **Great Indian Peninsula Railway**.
 
• The inaugural journey was attended by a large number of dignitaries and marked a significant milestone in India's transportation history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first train in India ran with **14 carriages** and carried about **400 passengers**.
 
• This event laid the foundation for the vast and extensive railway network that India has today.
 
• The introduction of the railway system in India had a profound impact on the country's economy and social structure, facilitating easier and faster movement of goods and people.
 
• Today, Indian Railways is one of the largest railway networks in the world, covering over **67,000 kilometers**.
 
• The railways play a crucial role in the daily commute of millions of people and the transportation of goods across the country.
